## 3.1 Single Document Insertion (insertOne())

> "insertOne(document) inserts a single document into a collection. If the collection doesn't exist yet, MongoDB creates it automatically."

- **Command Syntax & Polymorphic Data Types.** `db.<collectionName>.insertOne(<document>)` accepts a single document object (passing an array `[...]` throws an error). A single document can hold strings (`"Rahul"`), integers (`19`), arrays (`["Math", "Science"]`), booleans, and nested objects.
- **Primary Key Auto-Generation & Return Payload.** If the target collection does not exist, `insertOne()` creates it automatically. When `_id` is omitted, MongoDB generates a unique 12-byte `ObjectId` and returns `{ acknowledged: true, insertedId: ObjectId("...") }`.

```javascript
// Insert a single student document with string, numeric, and array fields
db.students.insertOne({
  name: "Rahul",
  age: 19,
  grade: 9,
  subjects: ["Math", "Science"]
});
// If "students" did not exist, MongoDB creates it automatically.
// Return Payload:
// {
//   acknowledged: true,
//   insertedId: ObjectId("6544b102c9e77c0012a40001")
// }
```

| Aspect | `db.collection.insertOne(document)` Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| Accepted Argument | Single object `{ key: value, ... }` (arrays rejected) |
| Missing Collection Behavior | Automatically creates the collection on write |
| Missing `_id` Behavior | Automatically generates a unique 12-byte `ObjectId` |
| Return Object | `{ acknowledged: true, insertedId: ObjectId("...") }` |

---

## 3.2 Batch Document Ingestion (insertMany())

> "insertMany([doc1, doc2, ...]) inserts multiple documents into a collection in a single call, passed as an array."

- **Command Syntax & Mandatory Array Wrapper (`[...]`) .** `insertMany()` strictly requires a JavaScript array (`[ { ... }, { ... } ]`) as its first parameter. Passing a single object without `[...]` throws a `MongoInvalidArgumentError`.
- **Single-Call Batching, Schema Flexibility & Return Payload.** All documents in the array are transmitted in one network call. Because MongoDB is schema-flexible, documents inside the same `insertMany()` batch can have different fields. The method returns `{ acknowledged: true, insertedIds: { '0': ObjectId(...), '1': ObjectId(...) } }`.

```javascript
// Batch insert multiple documents (notice heterogeneous fields in element 2)
db.students.insertMany([
  { name: "Meera", age: 17, grade: 7 },
  { name: "Kabir", age: 18, grade: 8, sports: ["Cricket"] }
]);
// Return Payload:
// {
//   acknowledged: true,
//   insertedIds: {
//     '0': ObjectId("6544b200c9e77c0012a40002"),
//     '1': ObjectId("6544b200c9e77c0012a40003")
//   }
// }
```

| Comparison Dimension | `insertOne(doc)` | `insertMany([doc1, doc2, ...])` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Parameter Type | Single Object `{ ... }` | Array of Objects `[ { ... }, { ... } ]` |
| Network Efficiency | `N` calls for `N` documents | `1` batched call for `N` documents |
| Schema Requirement | Flexible | Heterogeneous schemas allowed in same array |
| Return Telemetry | `{ acknowledged, insertedId }` | `{ acknowledged, insertedIds: { '0': ..., '1': ... } }` |

---

## Rapid Exam Trap Checklist

- **Trap 1 — Bracket Mismatch**: Passing an array `[...]` to `insertOne()` or passing comma-separated objects without `[...]` to `insertMany()` throws a syntax/type validation error.
- **Trap 2 — Return Key Naming**: `insertOne()` returns `insertedId` (singular), whereas `insertMany()` returns `insertedIds` (plural map indexed by position `'0'`, `'1'`, etc.).
- **Trap 3 — Schema Flexibility in Batches**: Documents inside the same `insertMany()` call do not need identical fields; MongoDB allows heterogeneous document shapes in the same collection.
